verdict.rationale: Vonage's docs cover creating sessions server-side (choosing media mode, one session per meeting or reusing it), server-generated JWT tokens that grant client SDK access, and official client libraries plus server-side SDKs. Community feedback calls the platform easy to implement. The evidence does not show tokens being scoped (roles, expiry or per-session limits), and it does not show a single short end-to-end quickstart linking all three steps. missing for 10: evidence of token scoping (roles/permissions/expiry), a documented short end-to-end quickstart flow, client-side connect code examples, independent hands-on corroboration of the full flow

support.subject: As a developer, I can create a session from my server, mint a scoped join token, and connect a client with the official SDK in a short documented flow

citations.quote: Server-generated Vonage Application JWT tokens grant client SDK access.
When you create a session, you specify how clients in the session will send audio-video streams, known as the media mode.
If your app connects users with one another for a one-time meeting, create a unique session for that meeting.
The platform includes client libraries for the web, mobile and desktop platform as well as server-side SDKs.
